description: A marathon early solo night at 19 Broadway in Fairfax — 34 songs mixing Hannan originals with a run of John Prine covers, two Cat Stevens songs, and a closing stretch of Irish traditionals.
Worthwhile note is the appearance yet again of Perfect Autumn Day.

Broadband noise reduction (noise reduction = 6dB, sensitivity = 5) was applied to the full recording in Audacity before the tracks were split, a first for the archive; and the individual tracks were then loudness-normalized to −20 LUFS. Fades and minor clip repairs were done by hand as usual.

description: Recorded directly from the soundboard to DAT at 19 Broadway in Fairfax. The full night has been split into its 31 individual songs — Jerry’s originals alongside traditional Irish songs and a handful of covers.
All 31 songs have now been volume-normalized for a consistent, comfortable listening level across the set.

A few of the songs here are obscure, unfinished sketches. “Loser,” “Xmas Song,” and “Blender” are short ideas more than full songs. “Dope World” may never have been finished, and “Slave Woman” was a very early song that — for obvious reasons — was rarely featured in live shows.
On the last song of the night, “The Old Triangle,” a guest singer named Johnny joins Jerry.

description: 19 Broadway is a small, famously loud bar in Fairfax, and this night was no exception — the room was packed and talking straight through the set. The tape was captured from the audience on a DAT recorder, so you’ll hear the crowd, the clink of glasses, and the bar’s heavy front door banging open and shut between songs.

Despite the racket, Sean played a long, generous set. The full tape has been split into its 31 individual songs — Sean’s originals alongside traditional tunes and a handful of covers. Each track streams here as a 320 kbps MP3, or can be downloaded as a lossless FLAC (password protected).
“Model Family Man” was originally written by the Hannans’ friend Paddy Nash in Ireland.

description: Unlike the audience tapes that make up most of this archive, this February 2000 set at 19 Broadway was recorded straight off the soundboard — so it’s unusually clean and close, with Sean’s voice and guitar right up front.

The tape has been split into its 11 songs — Sean’s originals alongside a few traditional Irish tunes and covers. Each track streams here as a 320 kbps MP3, or can be downloaded as a lossless FLAC (password protected).

In all this is a relatively short set for Sean. The tracks — both the streaming MP3s and the lossless FLAC files — have been loudness-normalized to −16 LUFS for a more even, consistent listening level.
On “Plastic Lemons” it is actually Jerry Hannan singing — he stepped in for a song while Sean, who was quite tired this night, took a break.
The full tape also includes some guitar music from an unidentified musician, and has not yet been fully audited.

Every performance has its own player and a link to that show.
